dedupe_keys.name: eureca energy urban resistance capacitance approach for urban building energy modelling

description: EUReCA, the Energy Urban Resistance Capacitance Approach, is an urban building energy modelling platform written entirely in Python for simulating and predicting the energy consumption of cities and urban areas. It builds bottom-up, simple dynamic resistance-capacitance models of each building, fed by an EPW weather file and spreadsheets of envelope types, operating schedules for occupancy, appliances, setpoints and HVAC use, and system types. It is developed by the BETALAB research group of the University of Padua, Italy, installs with pip from the GitHub repository and has documentation on Read the Docs; the last commit read is from April 2026 with tag v1.2.2. Coverage: any city with building geometry and typologies. Access: free on GitHub. Licence: GPL. Caveats: results depend on the typology and schedule spreadsheets the user prepares. Simulation uses are city-scale heating and cooling demand, retrofit and heat wave scenarios. Related records: EnergyPlus weather files and the Torino urban weather files.
inputs: Occupancy, appliance, setpoint and HVAC schedules
name: EUReCA: Energy Urban Resistance Capacitance Approach for urban building energy modelling
outputs: Hourly energy demand and consumption of each building in a city or district
